title: Token Fingerprint — Compact Cost Dashboard and Export Flow
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design a compact, shareable dashboard card and export workflow that surfaces token-level cost attribution with minimal cognitive load. The 'Token Fingerprint' view is intended for engineers and product owners who need a lightweight slice of token economics per route/session for quick triage, ad-hoc sharing, and CSV dumps for downstream finance tools. Scope: (1) a compact single-row card for list/table views with expandable details; (2) an export-first modal that maps cost attribution to customer billing fields; (3) lightweight inline explanations for quantization/batching adjustments; (4) accessibility and responsive behavior for small console panes. This ticket focuses exclusively on the visual/interaction design and the export schema; engineering integration work will be tracked in ENG dependents.
acceptance_criteria: A compact card design exists that fits a single console table row and shows: route, model, token-counts (in/out), per-unit USD, attribution breakdown (top-2 tags), and a 7-day sparkline.
Clicking the card expands an inline panel with a timeline, top contributing prompts, and a download/export CTA.
Export modal allows users to map internal attribution tags to billing fields and preview first 10 rows of CSV before download.
Design spec includes responsive states (desktop/tablet/mobile) and accessibility notes for keyboard navigation and screen readers.
Prototype links (Figma + interactive) are provided and a short usability script for a 5-minute moderated test is included.
Design handoff includes tokens, spacing, and component variants for engineering (small/regular/expanded).
comments: 2025-11-05 — Aisha: Drafted initial concept after reviewing console support requests for quick cost triage. Proposed a single-row compact card to fit existing usage tables.
2025-11-06 — Marco: Reviewed layout; requested inclusion of attribution tags and export mapping. Raised concern about row density on small screens.
2025-11-08 — Design critique: team prefers inline expand rather than full page drilldown to preserve flow. Suggested 7-day sparkline instead of full timeline by default.
2025-11-10 — PM review (Sofia): Prioritize export mapping to billing fields in this iteration; product suggests adding a 'confidence' indicator for attribution heuristics.
2025-11-11 — Accessibility review (Liam): Confirmed color contrast and keyboard-expandable rows; asked for aria labels on the export modal preview table.
2025-11-12 — Ready for handoff: prepared tokens and component variants; attached prototype and usability script for a 5-user unmoderated run.
decisions: Use compact single-row primary view with an inline expandable panel instead of a separate detail page to reduce context switches.
Show only top-2 attribution tags on compact card; full attribution list appears in expanded panel and export preview to reduce noise.
Export modal will be 'preview-first' (shows sample rows) and include a simple mapping UI to align attribution tags to billing line-item columns.
Default export CSV schema will include anonymized session IDs and a quantization_profile field so finance can reconcile unit variances.
Include a 'confidence' flag (low/medium/high) for attribution rows; this will help downstream consumers filter noisy attributions.
open_questions: How should we represent multi-model routing in a single row when a request falls back mid-invocation? (Design/engineering tradeoff)
Which subset of attribution tags should be lock-mapped to billing columns by default to minimize user configuration?
Do legal/privacy teams require additional anonymization beyond session_id hashing for exported CSVs?
Should the compact card show cost deltas vs previous period or keep focus on absolute per-row cost for clarity?
